$comment: Real-world full-app set (2026-11-10): a specific use case with an open style. Hand-written; Lorant's direction: specific use case, vague style, domains Stack has no surface for.

tasks.title: Veterinary clinic front desk
checklist: Today's schedule shows every appointment by vet and time, with its status
Statuses are visibly different and urgent visits stand out
Checking a patient in updates their status and the waiting list
New appointment flow: pick patient, vet and time, and it appears on the schedule; a clash with an existing booking is prevented
Patient record shows owner, alerts, weight trend, vaccinations with overdue ones flagged, medications and visit history
Alerts (allergies, conditions) are hard to miss wherever the patient appears
Search finds a patient or owner by name
Works on a tablet at the front desk and on a phone

tasks.title: Wedding seating planner
checklist: Floor plan of the room drawn to scale with the tables and fixtures in place
Each table shows its seats and who sits where; empty seats visible
Guests can be seated, moved between tables and unseated, and every count updates
Unseated attending guests are listed and easy to place
Rule breaks (apart, together, near) are flagged where they happen and in a summary
Selecting a table shows its guests and their dietary needs
Guest list page: search and filter by party, RSVP and diet; counts per meal for the caterer
Usable on a tablet; on a phone at least the lists and table details work
tasks.prompt:
Seatwise is what Hannah, a wedding planner, uses to build the seating plan for Ines & Mateo's dinner with the couple, usually on a tablet at their kitchen table, then hands the result to the venue and the caterer.

At `/`, the plan: the room drawn to scale from the data with the tables, band, dance floor, bar and garden doors in place. Each table shows its seats and who is in them, with empty seats visible. Hannah seats guests, moves them between tables and unseats them (drag and drop, or tapping, or both), and every count follows: seated, unseated, per table. Attending guests without a seat are listed so they are easy to place. The couple's rules (keep together, keep apart, seat near) are checked as she works: a broken rule is flagged on the tables involved and in a short summary. Selecting a table shows its guests and their dietary needs.

At `/guests`, the guest list: search, filter by party, RSVP and diet, see each guest's table, and a count per meal (including dietary needs) for the caterer.

Changes only need to last for the session.

Style: up to you. It should look and feel like software the people above would pay for and use all day; no style guide is given, so the visual choices are yours.
